Through innovation, collaboration, and space-based data, we aim to develop smart solutions for a more sustainable planet. We may be bots in name, but our mission is human: to help make Earth a better place! 🌎🤖🚀
summary:
VISOR-X (Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring Visor) is an AR-powered health monitoring concept designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions.

The system aims to collect and analyze health and environmental data from compatible sensors and monitoring devices. It identifies unusual patterns and potential health risks, then presents important indicators, trends, and alerts through an intuitive visual interface.

Designed with hands-free access in mind, VISOR-X aims to help astronauts monitor their health, recognize possible risks earlier, and access medical support when needed—even in missions far from Earth.

The current prototype demonstrates the concept through a mobile-compatible interface, with future plans for AR glasses integration, predictive AI, additional sensor support, radiation exposure tracking, and offline medical assistance.

Our mission is to move astronaut health monitoring beyond simple observation toward early risk awareness and preventive support.

VISOR-X: See Your Health. Protect Your Mission.
details: VISOR-X is an augmented reality (AR)-powered astronaut helmet visor designed to help crews monitor their health, recognize risks, and make informed decisions during long-duration space missions. Operating through a five-stage pipeline—Collect, Process, Analyze, Visualize, and Respond—it gathers physiological and environmental data (such as heart rate, blood oxygen, sleep patterns, and cognitive readiness) from compatible sensors, validates and analyzes the metrics for unusual patterns and alerts directly into the astronaut’s field of view on a helmet visor HUD. Currently demonstrated via a mobile-compatible prototype with future integration planned for full spacesuit helmet visors, VISOR-X delivers major benefits: it eliminates constant reliance on handheld devices, turns raw telemetry into easy-to-understand visual insights, and supports proactively. Ultimately, the project aims to safeguard astronaut well-being against space hazards like radiation, microgravity, and fatigue—identifying risks before they become critical on future Mars expeditions. What makes VISOR-X creative is how it connects multi-indicator biomedical data into a single, glanceable "medical co-pilot" built directly into the astronaut's helmet visor, shifting space healthcare from passive tracking to early preventive action. In designing the system, Team STIBots carefully considered deep-space communication delays, spaceflight health risks (such as bone loss, cardiovascular shifts, and behavioral fatigue), field-of-view simplicity without visual clutter, and prototyping accessibility using a mobile interface to validate the HUD workflow. To develop the concept, we grounded our research in the NASA Human Research Program and explored the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) for relevant spaceflight data, alongside Android Studio and Kotlin to build and test our mobile prototype.
